To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the main effects of a quantitative variable may be represented as a polynomial function; (ii) the main effect sum of square can be obtained by fitting a no-intercept polynomial to the cell means; (iii) this sum of squares is a sequential sum of squares, which can be obtained from a no-interceptor regression of the observation matrix on specially constructed independent matrices.

the main effect sum of squared deviations in a multi factor experiment with no interaction effects and no missing cells may be partitioned in a manner analogous to the partitioning of sums of squares in one way analysis of variance.
The main effects for a quantitative factor in a multi-factor experiment can be expressed as a linear or quadratic polynomial function of the factor levels.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of multi factor experiments when the factor of primary interest is quantitative and is measured on a continuous variable.
a method for fitting a polynomial to a main effect in a multi factor experiment.
the analysis of data from multi-factor experiments in which one of the factors, which we call the quantitative factor, is a quantitative variable.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the main effects for a factor which arises from distinct levels on a quantitative variable can be expressed as a linear combination of the levels of the quantitative factor, which may in turn be expressed as a weighted polynomial function of the levels.
this paper is a useful and practical contribution to the literature on analysis of variance of multi factor experiments with quantitative factors.

the method of fitting polynomials to the main effects in a multi factor experiment is a very useful technique which is easily performed with any statistical computing package and which can provide a very useful and convenient analysis of a multi factor experiment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed methodology is a very useful tool to analyze multi-factor experiments, especially when the factors of interest are quantitative.
it provides an efficient and simple method for the analysis of multi factor experiments when the factor of primary interest is a quantitative variable.
we provide a simple method of obtaining polynomial fits to main effects in factorial experiments when the factor of concern arises from a quantitative variable.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the analysis of multi factor experiments with a factor arising from a quantitative variable can be done with a no-intercept linear regression of the observation matrix on a specially constructed set of independent variables.

the use of polynomial regression is an effective and easy to use method for the analysis of main effects in multi-factor experiments, especially when there are no missing cells and the data are unbalanced.
the main effect of a factor in a factorial experiment can be modeled as a polynomial function.
